messages.subject: Model fit print-out inconsistency puzzle
parts:
I fit a simple unidimensional dichotomous (rasch and 2pl) model to my item response data (2800 persons by 26 items). The model fit outputs are a bit puzzling to me (parts highlighted in excerpts below).
For both the 1PL and 2PL model fits, the print-out of the model object gives RMSEA = 0, CFI = NaN, TLI = NaN, but model fit function M2( ) gives actual numbers.
What is the reason for the discrepancy? Much appreciate the help!

> mod.1pl <- mirt(cali.data, 1, itemtype='Rasch', TOL=.001, verbose=F)
> mod.1pl

Call:

    verbose = T)

Converged within 0.001 tolerance after 29 EM iterations.

BIC = 56792.99; SABIC = 56707.2
G2 (67108836) = 21984.64, p = 1
RMSEA = 0, CFI = NaN, TLI = NaN

> model.fit.1pl <- M2(mod.1pl)
> model.fit.1pl

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Model fit print-out inconsistency puzzle
parts:
The standard CFI/RMSEA are only computed when the table of complete responses is not sparse. For tests with more than even 5 items this is a pretty rare occurrence. You'd be best just to focus on the results from M2(). 

Phil
